correctness.rationale: The actual Smith inner recursion yields cubic error polynomial g3(z;alpha)=(1−alpha)z+alpha(1−alpha)z²+alpha²z³. J-conjugation on symmetric 2×2 matrices is an isometric self-adjoint involution with BOTH ±r eigenmodes, so the Frobenius worst-case factor is exactly max(|g3(r)|,|g3(−r)|). Directly rederived sums and derivatives: u+v=2r²alpha(1−alpha), u−v=2r(1−alpha+r²alpha²), u′=−r(1−r)(1+2r alpha), v′=r(1+r)(1−2r alpha). On alpha<0 the negative mode is worse than unrelaxed; alpha∈[0,1] cannot improve on r³. For r≥1/2 v is maximally negative at alpha=1 on the remaining ray; for 2/5≤r≤1/2 its stationary maximal value gives a global lower bound; for r≤2/5 equating negative mode values yields alpha_c and the two monotonic flanks. Equality and strictness at both interfaces check uniquely. Independent Sympy rederivation and 12 finite minimax grids passed. This does NOT optimize other spectral families, stagewise positivity or floating-point work.
risks: Finite minimax grids are not proof of all real alpha; analytic derivative inequalities supply completeness.
No positivity guarantee is made for intermediate overrelaxed matrices.

This solves an optimization left open at higher step count, not merely a polynomial substitution.

final_claim: For the two-state swap stochastic Lyapunov operator L_r(E)=rJEJ with 0<r<1 and symmetric Frobenius errors, the three-inner-stage Smith iteration has unique globally optimal real alpha at the sharp r=2/5 and r=1/2 transitions with minimax factors r²alpha(alpha−1), (3r−1)/4, r³, respectively.
limitations: Two-state swapping, 0<r<1, symmetric Frobenius error and a common real alpha; no arbitrary Lyapunov spectra, stagewise positivity or finite-precision conclusion.
